chk_problem.label: accurate
chk_problem.poster_evidence: Accurate T-staging is crucial for personalized treatment of laryngopharyngeal cancer. Early-stage disease is generally managed with organ-preserving surgery, laser resection, or definitive radiotherapy, whereas advanced disease often requires total laryngectomy and adjuvant treatment. Pathology-based staging is invasive and time-consuming, while manual review of an entire 3D CT volume is labor-intensive and subjective. Radiologists must track the tumor across many slices and assess extension into tightly packed adjacent structures, making borderline invasion particularly difficult to determine.

chk_primary_result.poster_evidence: Evaluation on 656 patients from four centers demonstrates consistent improvements over strong image-only and multimodal baselines in binary and three-class staging. A whole-volume CT baseline obtains 58.76% macro F1 for binary staging and 39.16% for three-class staging. Adding AOG raises performance to 77.96% and 52.80%, demonstrating the value of explicit anatomical relationship modeling. OCA produces 80.97% and 58.47%, confirming that organ-level alignment captures useful report evidence. Combining AOG and OCA yields 81.63% and 61.52%. The full model with REG reaches 83.96% binary F1 and 64.53% three-class F1, with the highest mean performance and lowest variance.

chk_conclusion.label: accurate
chk_conclusion.poster_evidence: We introduce an anatomy-structured multimodal framework that integrates 3D CT volumes and radiology reports for laryngopharyngeal cancer T-staging without manual tumor masks. AOG models clinically meaningful organ topology, OCA aligns each organ with relevant report evidence, and REG injects explicit invasion findings into graph reasoning while retaining anatomy-based risk connections. Evaluation on 656 patients from four centers demonstrates consistent improvements over strong image-only and multimodal baselines in binary and three-class staging. The model generalizes to external cohorts, remains robust to segmentation noise and report variation, and performs on par with or better than experienced radiologists. Its organ-level alignment and invasion pathways also provide clinically meaningful interpretability.
chk_conclusion.reason: The poster provides the substantive conclusion that the proposed framework outperforms baselines and radiologists, aligning with the reference.

chk_limitation.label: accurate
chk_limitation.poster_evidence: Error analysis identifies two dominant patterns. Nine of sixteen errors are over-staging cases, often caused by reports describing cartilage invasion that pathology does not confirm. Seven are under-staging cases, frequently associated with reports that omit invasion or state that invasion is absent despite pathological confirmation. These findings reflect inherent CT-pathology discordance rather than simple cross-modal misalignment and motivate uncertainty-aware fusion and clinical review of borderline cases.
chk_limitation.reason: The poster mentions the limitation of CT-based assessment, which can overestimate or underestimate tumor invasion, consistent with the reference.
